observation: Inspected the front, top and isometric views of the assembled set. Top view: the 7 by 9 field is complete with its cut grid; the twelve cocoa-brown belt tiles sit in two three-by-two blocks with file d left dry between them; the Sol star is the pale plinth at d1 ringed by three orange corona cells at c1, d2 and e1, and the Anti-Sol star is the black plug at d9 ringed by three cyan cells at c9, d8 and e9. All sixteen worlds are on their opening squares and each is the right planet on the right cell: Saturn a1 and Uranus g1, Earth b2 and Mars f2, Mercury a3, Neptune c3, Venus e3 and Jupiter g3, with the Anti-Sol eight mirrored through the board centre. Eight white discs read as bright coins and eight black discs as holes, so ownership separates at a glance. Isometric view: both stars show their two flames standing clear of the board border, the corona tongues stand at the outer corners of their own cells, the belt tiles show rubble around a smooth central pad, and the two gray trays sit clear of the field beyond the far edge. Front view: the size ladder is legible along one rank, the rank numerals read as dark digits on the white disc walls, and the star's flames rise above the crown of the smallest globe and below the crown of the largest. No missing, extra, misplaced or duplicated part; no visible interpenetration; no floating body; every piece sits flat on its own cell. One limitation of this render family, not of the geometry: the viewer treats the sealed colour channels as linear where the host and the shop read them as sRGB, so every colour previews lighter than the filament it names and the dark_gray board reads as mid gray here.
